Molecular weight, normal boiling point, Tc, Pc and acentric factor as given; standard liquid density: the saturated liquid at Tr = 0.7 (eq. 105, at the eq. 101 vapour pressure), because Tc lies below 288.7 K and no 60 F liquid exists; ideal-gas Cp eq. 16 (A=33071.93, B=-860.0281, C=12.22807, D=-0.000509703, E=1.628387e-7; data 50..1500 K) fitted by least squares as shifted_polynomial_5 over 104..900 K (33 points), largest deviation 0.546 % at 104.0 K, 0.152 % over 298.15..900 K; viscosity tables and freezing data in their entries. Imported by tools/compound-import.

fluid_domain.evidence: Fluid network only (not the column range): the ideal-gas Cp fit range, from max(ChemSep Cp data start, triple point) to 900 K; below it Cp is held and integrated, with a notice (a data-range end, never a validity floor). 100 Pa..2000000 Pa as the bundled light ends: PR78 from ChemSep critical constants, not qualified above that.

flammability.source: M. G. Zabetakis, Flammability Characteristics of Combustible Gases and Vapors, US Bureau of Mines Bulletin 627 (1965), Table A-1, p. 115, entry "Ethylene": L25 and U25 in air at 25 C and atmospheric pressure. A US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105). Constant with temperature (owner decision E23).

combustion.source: Hess's law on this record's thermochemistry (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1): the formula burnt to CO2, H2O (gas), SO2 and N2 on the ideal-gas heats of formation at 298.15 K of icheme:chemsep_carbon_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1), icheme:water (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1) and icheme:chemsep_sulfur_dioxide (chemsep-8.3-hf-r1). Computed by tools/heating-values/heating-values.mjs. Read by a fired heater's burners.
